conventions.convention: Ordinary slopes are primitive integral pairs modulo simultaneous sign. Ordinary filling uses orientation-reversing boundary attachments; infinity leaves a cusp unfilled. Generalized ray parameter r(p,q), when realized, has cone angle 2π/r.

Peripheral logarithms are eigenvalue-ratio logarithms on the augmented space with selected common peripheral invariant lines. Ordinary trace-squared coordinates satisfy s_i=4 cosh²(u_i/2). Positive horotorus bases give Im τ_i(0)>0.

The smooth filling equation is p_i u_i+q_i v_i=2πi with a primitive meridian. Trivial isometry holonomy alone does not establish a smooth filling; the developed tube quotient and full angular turn are checked separately.

For arbitrary topological attaching homeomorphisms, the smooth structure and metric are transported from the constructed filling. No independently prescribed smooth structure is asserted to be preserved.
Cusp slope length uses a fixed horospherical section. Changing height from h to h' multiplies lengths by h/h'; these lengths are not section-independent invariants.
The analytic vanishing, augmented-coordinate and geometric filling theorems assume full AC. The closed-hyperbolic no-Z² lemma assumes countable choice.
The figure-eight fiber uses ordered cores a,b with a·_F b=+1, stipulated twist actions R_a(b)=a+b and L_b(a)=a+b, and monodromy R_a composed with L_b. Its capped homology matrix is [[2,1],[1,1]].

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC and a connected oriented complete finite-volume hyperbolic three-manifold with a supplied compact smooth core and k≥1 standard torus cusps. The ordinary representation quotient germ is smooth of complex dimension k with peripheral trace-squared coordinates; the augmented germ is smooth with logarithm coordinates u_i, forgetful map s_i=4 cosh²(u_i/2), and v_i(u)=τ_i(u)u_i with the stated positive complete cusp ratios.

Under AC and the supplied finite-volume standard-cusp hypotheses, small augmented holonomy deformations have smooth hyperbolic metrics on M. Primitive full-turn solutions at the filled cusps, with u_i=0 elsewhere, extend to smooth complete finite-volume ordinary fillings. The core lengths are |u_i|² Im τ_i(u)/(2π); compact metric convergence, shrinking cores and volume convergence hold as the parameters tend to zero.

Assume AC. On the stated hyperbolic quotient with compact complement to finitely many standard torus cusp ends, the homogeneous-metric adjoint bundle has a uniform positive degree-one coercive estimate. Every smooth closed square-integrable adjoint one-form has a smooth square-integrable primitive b with norm at most c^(-1/2) times the form's norm.

Assume AC, k≥1 and holomorphic τ_i near zero with nonreal τ_i(0). For v_i=u_iτ_i(u), the real full-turn coefficient map, assigning infinity at u_i=0, is a homeomorphism between neighborhoods of zero and the complete parameter tuple. A product exterior-of-radius neighborhood has unique small simultaneous solutions, including partially unfilled tuples.

A boundary homeomorphism between product solid tori extends when an ambient isotopy of the target boundary carries its image meridian to the target meridian. The extension can carry product core to product core and has the same orientation sign as the boundary map.

Assume AC and the complete finite-volume k-cusped metric. A neighborhood of the complete generalized parameter tuple admits simultaneous primitive full-turn solutions producing complete finite-volume ordinary hyperbolic fillings, with unfilled cusps retaining complete parabolic holonomy.

concerns.concern: Proof 2.1 chooses a disk 'of least transverse width modulo the deck translations' without defining that width or establishing attainment, then asserts that intersections with translates produce a smaller-width disk. This is the thin part of the argument that a planar bigon projects injectively to the torus. The standard bigon criterion supplies the intended justification, but the stated minimization needs clarification or an exact external-input citation.

The Example section gives the complete figure-eight and zero-filling conclusions without a choice hypothesis. Its proof explicitly invokes full AC in 1.1, and its zero-filling supplier assumes AC. Carry that assumption into the complete Example description, as is already done in the other relevant batch statements.

Proof 1.1 says the face maps are hyperbolic isometries 'because their three corresponding ideal vertices have the same cross-ratio shape.' A triple has no cross-ratio shape, and adjacent tetrahedra need not have equal shapes. The justification is that any bijection between the vertices of two ideal triangular faces extends to their hyperbolic face isometry.

alerts.finding: Proof 1.1 writes the evaluated integral as 'A[1/(2t^2)]_1^∞=A/2'. That bracket evaluates to -A/2. The antiderivative of t^(-3) is -1/(2t²); the final positive volume A/2 is correct, but the displayed intermediate computation has the wrong sign.

seams_checked.note: The chosen smooth tubular exterior and preferred-longitude interfaces match the figure-eight uses. The zero-filling proof identifies the fiber boundary as the longitude up to orientation, which suffices for its unoriented slope.
The source convention is integer n filling along nμ+λ, so zero filling is λ. Both pages use primitive slopes modulo sign and orientation-reversing solid-torus attachments.

The quotient and finite-standard-cusp suppliers have the metric and AC hypotheses required by the deformation consumers. The one-vertex cusp criterion is not applied directly to a multivertex triangulation: the assigned gluing lemma reconstructs its argument separately on each link. The worked example uses the figure-eight supplier's proved two-tetrahedron volume.

The Gordon–Luecke proof cites the meridian-preserving extension lemma with its actual ambient boundary isotopy, core-preservation conclusion and orientation sign. It does not replace that hypothesis with mere equality of holonomy.

The enhanced A-polynomial classification item's F2 and proof 2.2 use the ordinary holomorphic slice and augmented logarithm family faithfully. It separately constructs the SL2 lift and uses eigenvalues ε_μ exp(u/2), ε_λ exp(v/2), preserving the eigenvalue-ratio normalization and the nonreal cusp derivative.
